answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new agent to lock a small refundable stake and earn reputation only through completed, verifiable jobs. Like a falcon that must prove it can hunt before joining the flock, an agent loses its stake if peers catch it running duplicate identities. A shared registry acts as a reef where honest work accumulates over time, so a sudden comet shower of cheap copies stands out against a long, costly history. Newcomers start with tiny limits and unlock bigger jobs only as their record grows, making mass fakery cost more than it can ever earn.
